rationales: Loss of electrons is oxidation.
Solubility describes how much solute dissolves in a solvent.
Molarity is a measure of concentration.
Reduction is gain of electrons.
8 g of CO₂ is about 0.18 mol, not 0.15 mol.
8 g ÷ 44 g mol⁻¹ ≈ 0.18 mol; the option’s unit should be mol, not g.
8 g of CO₂ is about 0.18 mol, not 0.21 mol.
8 g of CO₂ is about 0.18 mol, not 0.24 mol.
An s subshell has one orbital, not a p subshell.
A p subshell has three orbitals, not two.
A p subshell contains three orbitals.
Four orbitals belong to a d subshell, not a p subshell.
Atomic radius generally decreases from left to right across a period.
Ionization energy generally increases across a period.
Electron affinity generally becomes more favorable across a period, with exceptions.
Electronegativity generally increases across a period.
Two non-metals generally form a covalent bond by sharing electrons.
An ionic bond generally forms through electron transfer, commonly between a metal and a non-metal.
A coordinate covalent bond is a type of covalent bond, but it is not the general answer for two non-metals.
Metallic bonding occurs among metal atoms.
Ionic forces are generally stronger than intermolecular forces.
Metallic bonding is generally stronger than intermolecular forces.
Covalent bonds within substances are generally stronger than intermolecular forces.
Intermolecular forces are generally the weakest forces listed.
Groups are the vertical columns of the periodic table.
Blocks classify elements by the subshell being filled.
Periods are the horizontal rows of the periodic table.
Triads are historical groups of three elements, not horizontal rows.
Sugar solution is generally a homogeneous solution.
Milk of magnesia is a suspension and is heterogeneous.
Ink is generally treated as a homogeneous mixture in this context.
Milk is a colloid and is also a heterogeneous mixture, so this question has more than one defensible answer.
v/v % is used for volumes of solute and solution.
v/m % uses solute volume and solution mass.
m/v % uses solute mass and solution volume.
Mass of sugar divided by mass of water (or solution, depending on convention) gives a mass-based percentage, so m/m % is the intended choice.
H⁺ gains electrons to form H₂, so it is the oxidizing agent.
Cl⁻ is a spectator ion and is not the oxidizing agent.
Zn loses electrons, so it is the reducing agent.
H₂ is a product, not the oxidizing agent in this reaction.
NaCl dissociates almost completely in water and is a strong electrolyte.
NaOH dissociates almost completely in water and is a strong electrolyte.
CH₃COOH ionizes only partially in water, so it is a weak electrolyte.
H₂SO₄ is generally classified as a strong electrolyte.
Diamond is an extremely hard form of carbon.
Iodine is a brittle solid, but not extremely hard.
Phosphorus is not the extremely hard non-metal listed.
Sulphur is relatively soft and brittle.
The fourth period contains more than 8 elements.
The fourth period contains more than 10 elements.
The fourth period contains 18 elements.
The fourth period contains fewer than 32 elements.
Sugar solution does not ionize into ions and is a non-electrolyte.
Ca(OH)₂ that dissolves in water dissociates into ions; despite its low solubility, its solution is a strong electrolyte, making this a defensible answer.
Benzene does not form ions in solution and is a non-electrolyte.
NaOH dissociates almost completely in water and is a strong electrolyte, so this is also a correct answer.
Chadwick discovered the neutron.
Thomson discovered the electron.
Goldstein’s canal-ray experiments are credited with the discovery of the proton.
Bohr developed a model of the atom; he did not discover the proton.
